name: Inside Johnny: The Day Shift
summary: You lean in over Johnny's bed tray and drop onto a 1955 tin board game, where the night-shift foremen have hidden the parts of the Rumble, the machine that makes hunger. Give each of his classmates' crayon get-well cards to the part of him it was really written to, rebuild the Rumble from the assembly sheet, and turn it using last night's thermometer as the crank until the shift whistle blows and he asks for toast.
motifs: tin board game seen from inside
thread: Saturday, 7 a.m. With nothing left to guard, the night foremen read the class's get-well cards (Beverly's pudding, Eddie's kickball, Linda's hamster, Arthur's apology, Ronnie's crummy joke) and gave up the parts of the Rumble. You built it and cranked it with the shaken-down thermometer. The stomach rumbled, the shift whistle blew, Johnny asked for toast, and the sign now reads DAYS WITHOUT FEVER: 1. Carried: Mrs. Novak's note to Miss Halloran (he'll be back Tuesday) and a toast soldier, still warm. Unresolved: Tuesday, the walk back into class, the empty desk, and Arthur by the slide.
delight: A parent's real moment of relief isn't the thermometer, it's the child saying they're hungry. I loved making that moment a factory shift whistle powered by five clumsy, kind letters from eight-year-olds. Dov the sump man reading Arthur's apology for the sneeze on the slide ('I'm not crying. It's the sump.') is my favourite line, along with the assembly sheet's 'Crank: not supplied. Any straight thing of the right length will do.'

idea.name: Inside Johnny
idea.premise: A 1950s tin board game set inside a sick boy's body, where a crew of gruff foremen run his organs as factory departments. After the fever comes recovery, one game at a time: the night shift that fought the fever has to become a day shift that rebuilds an ordinary day, and the outside world reaches in through small kindnesses like a mother's comforts, a class's cards and a note to school.
